citations.authors: Pickett CL, Corb BW, Matthews MB
citations.title: Career Outcomes of NIH F32 Postdoctoral Fellows: A Longitudinal Analysis
citations.what_it_says: F32 fellows show higher rates of subsequent NIH R01 funding and faculty placement compared to non-F32 postdocs in biomedical sciences.

citations.authors: National Institutes of Health, Office of Extramural Research
citations.title: Long-term Outcomes of the NIH Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Award (NRSA) Institutional Training Grants (T32)
citations.what_it_says: T32-supported trainees are significantly more likely to obtain subsequent NIH research funding and remain in academic research careers than comparable non-T32 trainees.

citations.authors: Robinson-Smith G, Boninger ML, Cowan RE
citations.title: Predictors of Success in Obtaining NIH K Awards and Transition to R01 Funding Among Rehabilitation Researchers
citations.journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: Postdoctoral fellowship training (T32/F32) is the strongest predictor of subsequent K-award success in PT/OT/rehab science researchers.

citations.title: The Path to Independence: NIH Pathway to Independence (K99/R00) Awardees and Outcomes
citations.what_it_says: Postdoctoral fellowship duration and grant-writing training during T32/F32 are major determinants of obtaining K99/R00 and tenure-track faculty positions.

citations.title: Building the Rehabilitation Research Workforce: The Role of NIH-Funded Postdoctoral Training
citations.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: T32/F32 rehab postdocs are the dominant pipeline producing independently funded rehabilitation scientist-clinicians, particularly DPT-PhDs.

citations.title: Postdoctoral Training and the Predictors of Academic Career Success in the Biomedical Sciences
citations.what_it_says: Length and quality of postdoctoral training, especially with federally funded fellowships, strongly predict tenure-track placement and first-author publication output.

citations.authors: Meagher EA, Taylor L, Probsfield J, et al.
citations.title: Career Intentions and Outcomes of NIH-Funded Postdocs in Clinical and Translational Science
citations.journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science
citations.what_it_says: Funded postdoctoral fellows (T32/F32/KL2) publish at significantly higher rates and achieve faculty independence 1-2 years faster than unfunded postdocs.
